rubric.why: The elements are arranged by increasing atomic number, and their properties recur in that arrangement.
rubric.how: Award for stating that properties recur when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.

rubric.why: The recurrence of similar outer-shell electron configurations accounts for the repeated properties.
rubric.how: Award for linking the repetition to the recurrence of similar outer-shell electron configurations.

modelAnswer: When elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, their properties recur after regular intervals.
This periodic repetition occurs because similar outer shell electron configurations recur.

items.followUp: Explain why water molecules attract one another through dipole–dipole forces.

rubric.why: Chlorine attracts the shared electron pair more strongly than hydrogen, making HCl polar.
rubric.how: Award for identifying HCl as polar and relating this to chlorine's stronger attraction for the shared electrons.

rubric.why: Oppositely charged ends of neighboring HCl molecules attract one another.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the partial positive end of one HCl molecule attracts the partial negative end of another.

modelAnswer: HCl is a polar molecule because chlorine attracts the shared electron pair more strongly than hydrogen.
The partial positive end of one HCl molecule attracts the partial negative end of another, producing dipole–dipole forces.

items.followUp: What is a saturated solution? How can it be made unsaturated?

rubric.why: An unsaturated solution contains less dissolved solute than the maximum amount possible at that temperature.
rubric.how: Award for defining it as containing less than the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a specified temperature.

rubric.why: Adding solute increases the dissolved amount until the solution reaches its saturation limit.
rubric.description: Changing it to a saturated solution
rubric.how: Award for stating that more solute is added until no more dissolves at that temperature.

modelAnswer: An unsaturated solution contains less solute than the maximum amount that can dissolve at a given temperature.
It can be changed into a saturated solution by adding more solute until no more dissolves at that temperature.

items.followUp: What compounds are formed when lithium and sodium react with oxygen?

rubric.why: Group I metals react with oxygen to form oxides or related oxygen compounds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that Group I metals react with oxygen to form oxygen compounds.

rubric.why: The characteristic products include lithium oxide, sodium peroxide and potassium superoxide.
rubric.how: Award for giving at least one correct product formula for a Group I metal reacting with oxygen.

modelAnswer: Group I metals react with oxygen to form oxides or related oxygen compounds.
Lithium forms Li2O, sodium forms Na2O2, and potassium forms KO2.
